featured_reviews.review_text:
As an ASCA (Australian Strength and Conditioning Association) accredited coach and a former professional athlete, I have trained across various Cult/Gold’s franchises. The Powai branch is, without a doubt, the worst-managed premium gym I have ever encountered. It is a service business with zero concept of safety, hospitality, or basic fitness standards.

Here is why you should avoid this facility until corporate management intervenes:

Severe Safety Hazards & Poor Maintenance: Brand new machines are malfunctioning within a week of arrival, and older equipment (like the Smith machine) is left neglected. Worse, they perform heavy industrial maintenance—like drilling into the floor and cutting metal with power saws—directly on the gym floor during peak operational hours. The flying sparks, noise, and toxic dust are an absolute health and safety violation.

Substandard, Unqualified Trainers: The gym boasts about its "Elite" status, but the trainers (including the Head Trainer) completely lack basic knowledge of biomechanics, core stability, or proper form. They ignore members executing dangerous movements, prioritizing casual chit-chat over client safety. They also refuse to follow their own rules—never re-racking weights or using sweat towels.

Hypocritical Management & Rules: The personal trainers hoard the member lockers for themselves, forcing paying clients to dump their personal belongings on workout benches.

When you confront the staff or ask to speak to a senior manager, you are met with zero accountability and a complete lack of professionalism.

Buying a space in a prime locality and putting up a premium brand name means nothing if your service is toxic and your staff is incompetent. Save your money and your physical health—do not join this branch until they overhaul their staff and management. Corporate needs to pull the CCTV footage immediately and fix this mess.

I would rather suggest to use it once or twice if you’re travelling to Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Aakash Pandey
featured_reviews.review_text:
Okay. So I have gone through a fair number of reviews and I feel most criticisms are unfair. Let me write a detailed review.

IT IS A TOP GYM.

In my personal experience, literally everything that you need from a gym is available here.

Staff: Yes, a few trainers won't pay much attention to you but that's the difference. There are floor trainers for assisting you and Personal trainers for PT. Still, if you approach them, they will correct your posture or ask someone to help you.

Someone mentioned trainers with bellies!! I have seen these guys train during non peak hours, they are literally beasts. Those are some heavy lifters. They tend to have a bit of a ponch but they are very well versed in their knowledge of body building and fitness. And hardly 1 or 2 of them have it. I don't know who they saw.

Equipment; Top class, well maintained. They have ENOUGH equipment and with the new renovation, there is MORE THAN SUFFICIENT space in the gym. Best quality equipment that I have ever seen. They have enough cardio machines too.

Crowd: Yes, it gets crowded between 6 - 9 pm. But that's cause it's  a really good gym. And all gyms get crowded in those hours. At least all the good ones. Go in non peak hours if the crowd's a problem for you. I have seen some really motivated and dedicated bunch of people here as well. It keeps you coming back for more as well.

Music: You sometimes won't even need your own music. It's that good.

Hygiene: Cannot complain. Could be a bit better in the men's changing rooms but then it's not the staff but people who don't follow basic etiquette to be blamed. They try their best to keep it up to the mark at all times.

TL:DR. Just join the gym. It is GREAT.

featured_reviews.name: Siddharth Chandrashekar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Been using this gym for around 5 months, it's been pretty solid. I've used a few gyms in ghatkoparl/chembur which were good, but there was always a trade off - this gym is large, clean and has a good variety of equipment.

Some of the equipment are a little old but there is enough new equipment to hit every muscle group.

It is really crowded during peak hours so I prefer either going early in the morning or, if I can, around 2-4pm. 9pm is somehow the busiest time I've seen.

The only equipment issue I've had were the treadmills getting stuck a little but they seem to be trying to fix it, when I first joined this wasn't a problem but I've noticed a lot of machines had the issue. But slowly I've seen them go out of order and then come back working ok.

The last thing is the bathroom/shower for the men's area at least is in good condition, I've tried 3 gyms in mumbai and this is the best one so far. The 2 in chembur/ghatkopar were not bad but I tried a gym in Malad and it was awful. I've showered here almost everyday for months with no issues, the staff clean it after every shower.

The AC seemed bad for a few weeks in the middle but it seems to be fixed now.

Overall, it isn't a brand but it's the best I've seen in mumbai so far.

A strong core is the foundation of almost every movement we make, acting as a stabilizer for the spine and a powerhouse for daily activities.
Here are five effective exercises to build core strength and stability:
Plank: A fundamental move for total core engagement. Hold a push-up position with your weight on your forearms or hands, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Dead Bug: Excellent for stabilizing the spine. Lie on your back with arms up and knees at a 90^\circ angle. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed firmly against the ground.
Bird-Dog: Enhances balance and back strength. Start on all fours; extend your right arm forward and your left leg back simultaneously. Hold briefly, then switch sides.
Glute Bridge: While often seen as a leg exercise, it is vital for the posterior core. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, then lift your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Side Plank: Targets the obliques and lateral stability. Propped up on one forearm, lift your hips so your body forms a diagonal line, holding the position without letting your hips sag.
Consistency is key to seeing results and preventing injury. If you are struggling with form or require a personalized rehabilitation plan, please call us to schedule a physical therapy consultation.

Strengthen Your Core: Your abdominal and back muscles act as a natural brace for your spine. Incorporating basic movements like planks or bird-dogs helps stabilize your lower back and reduces the risk of injury.

A strong core is the foundation of almost every movement we make, acting as a stabilizer for the spine and a powerhouse for daily activities.
Here are five effective exercises to build core strength and stability:
Plank: A fundamental move for total core engagement. Hold a push-up position with your weight on your forearms or hands, keeping your body in a straight line from head to heels.
Dead Bug: Excellent for stabilizing the spine. Lie on your back with arms up and knees at a 90^\circ angle. Slowly lower the opposite arm and leg toward the floor while keeping your lower back pressed firmly against the ground.
Bird-Dog: Enhances balance and back strength. Start on all fours; extend your right arm forward and your left leg back simultaneously. Hold briefly, then switch sides.
Glute Bridge: While often seen as a leg exercise, it is vital for the posterior core. Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat, then lift your hips toward the ceiling until your body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees.
Side Plank: Targets the obliques and lateral stability. Propped up on one forearm, lift your hips so your body forms a diagonal line, holding the position without letting your hips sag.
